paragraphs.title: Noah and His Family Are Commanded to Enter the Ark

easy.question: Who was commanded to enter the ark with his household?
answers: Noah and his household
Noah alone
Everyone of that generation
easy.explanation: The Lord said to Noah, “Come thou and all thy house into the ark.”

easy.question: How many pairs of clean animals was Noah commanded to take?
answers: One pair
Seven pairs
Forty pairs
easy.explanation: Noah was told to take clean animals “by sevens,” meaning seven pairs.

easy.question: How long would the rain fall on the earth?
answers: Seven days
Seventy days
Forty days and forty nights
easy.explanation: The Lord said that He would cause it to rain for forty days and forty nights.

medium.question: Why did the Lord command Noah specifically to enter the ark?
answers: Because the Lord saw that he was righteous in his generation
Because Noah had built the largest city
Because Noah was king of the earth
medium.explanation: The Lord said, “For thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation.”

medium.question: What is the correct order of events in these verses?
answers: The rain fell, Noah entered, and then the animals were brought in
Noah was commanded to enter, told to bring in the animals, and warned about the rain
Noah brought in the animals, the rain fell, and then the Lord commanded him to enter
medium.explanation: First Noah was commanded to enter the ark, then to bring in the animals, and finally he was told about the coming rain.

medium.question: In the phrase “every living substance that I have made,” what does “living substance” refer to?
answers: The ark alone
The rain falling from heaven
All living creatures made on the earth
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to all living things that God had made and that would be destroyed from the earth.

challenge.question: What was the difference between the number of clean and unclean animals Noah was to take?
answers: Seven pairs of clean animals and one pair of unclean animals
One pair of clean animals and seven pairs of unclean animals
Only seven animals of every kind
challenge.explanation: The command distinguishes between clean animals, taken by sevens, and unclean animals, taken by twos.

challenge.question: Why does the verse say that the animals were taken “the male and his female”?
answers: To distinguish large animals from small ones
So they could reproduce and preserve their species
So that each animal would have a separate place in the ark
challenge.explanation: The male and female were taken together “to keep seed alive,” allowing the species to continue.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that birds, not only land animals, were brought into the ark?
answers: The mention of forty days and forty nights
The statement that Noah was righteous
The command to take birds of the air as well
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly says, “Of fowls also of the air,” showing that birds were included.

questions.question: What was the difference between the number of clean and unclean animals Noah was to take?
answers: Seven pairs of clean animals and one pair of unclean animals
One pair of clean animals and seven pairs of unclean animals
Only seven animals of every kind
questions.explanation: The command distinguishes between clean animals, taken by sevens, and unclean animals, taken by twos.

questions.question: Why does the verse say that the animals were taken “the male and his female”?
answers: To distinguish large animals from small ones
So they could reproduce and preserve their species
So that each animal would have a separate place in the ark
questions.explanation: The male and female were taken together “to keep seed alive,” allowing the species to continue.

questions.question: Which detail shows that birds, not only land animals, were brought into the ark?
answers: The mention of forty days and forty nights
The statement that Noah was righteous
The command to take birds of the air as well
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly says, “Of fowls also of the air,” showing that birds were included.

paragraphs.title: Noah, His Family, and the Animals Enter the Ark

easy.question: How old was Noah when the flood came?
answers: Six hundred years old
One hundred years old
Seven years old
easy.explanation: The verse says that Noah was six hundred years old when the floodwaters were upon the earth.

easy.question: Who entered the ark with Noah?
answers: His sons alone
His sons, his wife, and his sons’ wives
Everyone on earth
easy.explanation: Noah entered with his sons, his wife, and his sons’ wives.

easy.question: How many animals of each kind came to Noah?
answers: One
Three
Two
easy.explanation: The verse says that they entered “two and two,” the male and the female.

medium.question: Why did Noah and his family enter the ark?
answers: Because of the floodwaters
To look for food
To build a house
medium.explanation: They entered the ark in order to be saved from the floodwaters.

medium.question: What order of events is described in these verses?
answers: The flood began, and then Noah entered the ark
Noah and his family entered, the animals came, and after seven days the floodwaters came upon the earth
The animals came after the flood had ended
medium.explanation: First Noah and his family entered, then the animals came, and after seven days the floodwaters covered the earth.

medium.question: In the phrase “every thing that creepeth upon the earth,” what does “creepeth” mean?
answers: Flies in the sky
Lives in the water
Moves or crawls on the ground
medium.explanation: In this context, “creepeth” refers to creatures that move or crawl on the ground.

challenge.question: What can we understand from the fact that the animals entered “the male and the female”?
answers: They entered as pairs that could preserve their species
There were only male animals
Each animal entered alone
challenge.explanation: “The male and the female” indicates a pair of each kind, so the species could continue.

challenge.question: What connection is there between verse 6 and verses 7–10?
answers: Noah was six hundred only after the flood
Noah was six hundred when he entered the ark and the flood took place
Noah entered the ark when he was seven years old
challenge.explanation: Verse 6 gives Noah’s age, and the following verses describe his entering the ark and the beginning of the flood at that time.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “after seven days” emphasize?
answers: That the flood lasted only seven days
That Noah stayed in the ark for seven years
That the floodwaters came upon the earth after seven days
challenge.explanation: The phrase says that after seven days the floodwaters were upon the earth; it does not say the flood lasted only seven days.

questions.question: What can we understand from the fact that the animals entered “the male and the female”?
answers: They entered as pairs that could preserve their species
There were only male animals
Each animal entered alone
questions.explanation: “The male and the female” indicates a pair of each kind, so the species could continue.

questions.question: What connection is there between verse 6 and verses 7–10?
answers: Noah was six hundred only after the flood
Noah was six hundred when he entered the ark and the flood took place
Noah entered the ark when he was seven years old
questions.explanation: Verse 6 gives Noah’s age, and the following verses describe his entering the ark and the beginning of the flood at that time.

questions.question: What does the phrase “after seven days” emphasize?
answers: That the flood lasted only seven days
That Noah stayed in the ark for seven years
That the floodwaters came upon the earth after seven days
questions.explanation: The phrase says that after seven days the floodwaters were upon the earth; it does not say the flood lasted only seven days.

paragraphs.title: The Fountains of the Deep and the Windows of Heaven Open

easy.question: How long did the rain fall on the earth?
answers: Forty days and forty nights
Seven days
One hundred days
easy.explanation: Verse 12 says that the rain was upon the earth forty days and forty nights.

easy.question: Who entered the ark with Noah?
answers: His sons alone
His family and the animals
Everyone on earth
easy.explanation: Noah, his wife, his sons, his sons’ wives, and the animals entered the ark.

easy.question: How did the animals enter the ark?
answers: In pairs, male and female
Each one alone
Only male animals
easy.explanation: The verses say that they entered two by two, male and female.

medium.question: What caused the waters to come from both the earth and the sky?
answers: Noah opened the ark
The fountains of the deep broke up and the windows of heaven opened
The animals brought in water
medium.explanation: Verse 11 says that the fountains of the great deep broke up and the windows of heaven were opened.

medium.question: In the phrase “the windows of heaven were opened,” what does “windows” mean?
answers: Openings or windows in heaven
Small clouds
Large rivers
medium.explanation: The context says that the windows opened and rain fell, so the word refers to openings through which the waters came.

medium.question: What order of events is described in these verses?
answers: The rain stopped, and then Noah entered the ark
Noah entered the ark, and then the rain began to fall
The animals left, and then the ark was built
medium.explanation: The verses describe Noah, his family, and the animals entering, followed by the Lord shutting them in.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the repeated phrase “after his kind” in the description of the animals?
answers: Different kinds of animals were in the ark
Only birds were in the ark
All the animals were identical
challenge.explanation: The repeated phrase emphasizes that animals of many different kinds entered the ark.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “in the selfsame day” mean in verse 13?
answers: On the following night
On that very same day
After forty years
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that Noah entered the ark on that exact day.

challenge.question: What can we understand from the fact that the Lord shut the ark after everyone entered?
answers: They entered according to the command, and the Lord separated those in the ark from the outside
Noah forgot to shut the ark
The flood had already ended
challenge.explanation: Verse 16 says that they entered as God had commanded, and then the Lord shut Noah in.

questions.question: What can we infer from the repeated phrase “after his kind” in the description of the animals?
answers: Different kinds of animals were in the ark
Only birds were in the ark
All the animals were identical
questions.explanation: The repeated phrase emphasizes that animals of many different kinds entered the ark.

questions.question: What does the phrase “in the selfsame day” mean in verse 13?
answers: On the following night
On that very same day
After forty years
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that Noah entered the ark on that exact day.

questions.question: What can we understand from the fact that the Lord shut the ark after everyone entered?
answers: They entered according to the command, and the Lord separated those in the ark from the outside
Noah forgot to shut the ark
The flood had already ended
questions.explanation: Verse 16 says that they entered as God had commanded, and then the Lord shut Noah in.

paragraphs.title: The Waters Rise and the Ark Floats

easy.question: How many days was the flood upon the earth?
answers: Forty days
Fifteen days
Seven days
easy.explanation: Verse 17 says that the flood was forty days upon the earth.

easy.question: What did the waters do to the ark?
answers: They immediately sank it
They carried it and lifted it above the earth
They returned it to the mountain
easy.explanation: The waters carried the ark, and it was lifted above the earth.

easy.question: What did the waters cover according to these verses?
answers: Only the valleys
Only the cities
All the high mountains
easy.explanation: Verse 19 says that the waters covered all the high hills under the whole heaven.

medium.question: What happened as the waters increased and rose?
answers: The ark stopped on the ground
The ark was lifted up and moved across the waters
The mountains became higher
medium.explanation: As the waters increased, they carried the ark, and it moved upon the surface of the waters.

medium.question: In the phrase “it was lift up above the earth,” what happened to the ark?
answers: It broke apart
It disappeared
It rose upward
medium.explanation: The phrase means that the ark was lifted or raised above the earth by the waters.

medium.question: What does verse 20 teach about the height of the waters relative to the mountains?
answers: The waters rose fifteen cubits above the mountains
The waters reached only the bottom of the mountains
The waters fell fifteen cubits below the mountains
medium.explanation: Verse 20 says that the waters prevailed fifteen cubits upward and covered the mountains.

challenge.question: Why does the verse emphasize that the waters covered “all the high hills under the whole heaven”?
answers: To say that only one mountain was covered
To describe shallow waters
To emphasize that the entire earth was covered
challenge.explanation: The broad wording emphasizes that no high mountains remained uncovered.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the order of events in verses 17–20?
answers: The waters continued rising until they passed over the height of the mountains
The waters fell immediately after the flood began
The ark sank before the waters increased
challenge.explanation: First the waters lifted the ark, then they covered the mountains, and finally they rose fifteen cubits above them.

challenge.question: What does the repeated description that the waters “prevailed” emphasize?
answers: That the waters stopped in one place
That the waters grew stronger and rose higher and higher
That the waters began to dry up
challenge.explanation: The repeated wording, including “prevailed exceedingly,” emphasizes the continued rise and power of the waters.

questions.question: Why does the verse emphasize that the waters covered “all the high hills under the whole heaven”?
answers: To say that only one mountain was covered
To describe shallow waters
To emphasize that the entire earth was covered
questions.explanation: The broad wording emphasizes that no high mountains remained uncovered.

questions.question: What can we infer from the order of events in verses 17–20?
answers: The waters continued rising until they passed over the height of the mountains
The waters fell immediately after the flood began
The ark sank before the waters increased
questions.explanation: First the waters lifted the ark, then they covered the mountains, and finally they rose fifteen cubits above them.

questions.question: What does the repeated description that the waters “prevailed” emphasize?
answers: That the waters stopped in one place
That the waters grew stronger and rose higher and higher
That the waters began to dry up
questions.explanation: The repeated wording, including “prevailed exceedingly,” emphasizes the continued rise and power of the waters.

paragraphs.title: The Flood Covers the Earth and Noah Remains in the Ark

easy.question: What happened to all flesh that lived on the earth?
answers: It died
It fled
It entered a city
easy.explanation: The verses say that all flesh, including animals and human beings, died.

easy.question: Who remained alive after the flood?
answers: All human beings
Noah and those with him in the ark
Only the animals
easy.explanation: The text says, “Noah only remained alive, and they that were with him in the ark.”

easy.question: How long did the waters prevail upon the earth?
answers: Forty days
Seven days
One hundred and fifty days
easy.explanation: Verse 24 says that the waters prevailed upon the earth for one hundred and fifty days.

medium.question: What does the list of creatures that died show about the extent of the flood?
answers: The flood affected every kind of creature on the earth
The flood affected only human beings
The flood affected only water animals
medium.explanation: The list includes birds, cattle, beasts, creeping things, and human beings, showing the flood’s enormous scope.

medium.question: In the sentence “all flesh died,” what does “died” mean?
answers: Was born
Ceased to live
Disappeared from sight
medium.explanation: In the context of the flood, “died” means that the living creatures ceased to live.

medium.question: What is the connection between the creatures’ deaths in verse 21 and Noah’s survival in verse 23?
answers: Noah left the ark before they died
The other creatures hid in the ark
Their deaths emphasize that only Noah and those with him in the ark were saved
medium.explanation: The text first describes the death of all other creatures and then emphasizes that only Noah and those with him remained alive.

challenge.question: Who is included in the phrase “all in whose nostrils was the breath of life”?
answers: All living creatures outside the ark that breathed
Human beings alone
The birds of the air alone
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to every creature with the breath of life that was on the dry land outside the place of rescue.

challenge.question: What does the word “only” emphasize in “Noah only remained alive”?
answers: That Noah was the last to leave the ark
That only Noah and those with him were saved
That Noah had no animals with him
challenge.explanation: The word “only” highlights the sole exception: Noah and those with him in the ark remained alive.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the statement that the waters prevailed for another 150 days after the creatures died?
answers: The flood ended immediately after their deaths
The waters were found only inside the ark
The waters continued to dominate the earth even after the destruction
challenge.explanation: Verse 24 continues describing the power of the waters, showing that the flood still covered the earth after the creatures had died.

questions.question: Who is included in the phrase “all in whose nostrils was the breath of life”?
answers: All living creatures outside the ark that breathed
Human beings alone
The birds of the air alone
questions.explanation: The phrase refers to every creature with the breath of life that was on the dry land outside the place of rescue.

answers: That Noah was the last to leave the ark
